turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Please sit. Blood pressure is one oh nine over seventy-seven. Pulse ninety-six, ah sorry, eighty-two.
[SEG0002] person_1 (NURSE): Temperature is thirty-eight point three. Weight today is seventy-four kilos. Last time in March you were sixty-eight. Your last pressure was one-forty.
[SEG0003] person_2 (PATIENT): Seventy-four? Ugh, it is the mithai from my cousin's sangeet, three types, I could not stop. And uh this humidity is making my face so oily.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): Temperature is thirty-eight point three, a bit high. Any fever feeling, cough, or body pain?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no fever feeling, no cough, no body pain. I was standing in the hot sun only, I feel fine.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Then what is the problem today?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, basically the pimples will not go, and my periods are all over the place. There is hair coming on my chin also, so embarrassing, and I have put on weight.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Pimples since how long?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Err, the bad ones, about two years. Periods went irregular around then, in second year of college. Chin hair is newer, like six months only.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Gap between the periods?

[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Sometimes nothing for two months, sometimes it comes in three weeks. Last one, umm, I can't remember the date, maybe six weeks back. I deleted that period app, it kept nagging.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Pain in the menses, yes or no?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No. They are light actually, not painful.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any white discharge or itching?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No discharge, no itching. My roommate said try ice on the face, I did, total waste of time.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Weight gain is how much?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): From sixty-eight in March to seventy-four now, so six kilos. I stopped my evening walks after the final exams. Canteen samosas did the rest, obviously.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): More thirst? Passing more urine?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No, thirst is normal and toilet is normal. I just drink chai all day, that is a whole hobby.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Diabetes in the family?

[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): My mother had diabetes. She takes metformin, Glycomet, five hundred I think, every day. My sister is ok, she only eats biotin gummies, pink bottle, for her hair fall, which is not even my problem.

[SEG0022] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Mm. Doctor, I stay in the house with her, and she skips breakfast most days. She is twenty-two only. Her mother told me on the phone, no hormone tablets until tests are done.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): You yourself, any daily tablets?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing daily. I took one Crocin last month for a headache, that is all, not regular.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any reaction to a medicine, ever? Penicillin?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No, never, I have taken penicillin and everything. Amoxicilin last year for a throat infection, completely fine, no rash, nothing.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): You smoke? Alcohol?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Never smoked. Alcohol, maybe a sip at weddings, not really. My lehenga fitting is next Sunday and the blouse is already tight, that is the real crisis.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): I am seeing comedones and pustules on both cheeks, and coarse hair on the chin. Abdomen I am not examining today.

[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): I will start you on the combined pill, cyproterone two milligrams with ethinylestradiol, Diane, one tablet daily for twenty-one days then a break. Blood tests we can do later.

[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh wait, um, I should have said, I get headaches with sparkly zigzag lights, about once a month, since college. My roommate says that is migraine aura, is the pill ok with that? It freaks me out in class.

[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): With visual aura I will not start the combined pill. No hormone tablet today. We will do fasting glucose, TSH and serum testosterone, and a pelvic ultrasonography. Kindly come after two weeks with the reports.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh. Right. Needles though, ugh, and is the scan the cold gel one?

[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ultrasound is gel only, on the lower abdomen, no needle. The blood test is one fasting sample. Kindly walk thirty minutes daily and cut the sweets. Do not take your sister's biotin.
[SEG0035] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I will see that she walks. Her mother also had sugar in pregnancy, she keeps worrying it will come to this girl.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any operation in the past?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no operation. Well actually a wisdom tooth, they just pulled it, does that count, nothing major.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Bowels, any problem?
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): No, bowels are fine. Every morning, very regular, unlike the periods.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): Acne, irregular cycles, chin hair and weight gain, I suspect polycystic ovary syndrome. A thyroid problem is also possible. I am not confirming either one today.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Ok. My friend with that PCOD thing did laser and she is fine in photos, I just don't want a beard at the wedding. Thank you, we will do the tests.
[SEG0042] person_1 (NURSE): Fasting means only water from tonight. The blood test is at 8 in the morning, counter is on the left.

spec.situation: Young woman with acne and irregular periods for two years, some facial hair, weight gain; mother had diabetes; bloods and pelvic scan planned; contraceptive pill discussed, not started.

traps.happens: The nurse reads vital signs aloud in spoken words ('one oh nine over seventy-seven', 'thirty-eight point three') and also gives a PRIOR value ('last time in March you were sixty-eight', 'your last pressure was one-forty'). Someone may also correct a reading.
traps.label_rule: vital_signs hold only the CURRENT measured values, written normally (109/77, 38.3, 52 kg). The prior value is NOT a vital sign; it is recorded in the weight/BP entry's own notes only if the schema allows, otherwise omitted. Every number must be exactly as said; never invent or round a value that was not said.

traps.happens: The doctor asks about drug reactions. Variants (use ONE per encounter): (a) the patient says 'No, never, I have taken penicillin and everything' (no allergy); (b) the patient is unsure ('maybe the antibiotic or the painkiller, nobody told me which'); (c) a real allergy with the reaction described; (d) allergies are never asked.
traps.label_rule: (a) NO allergy entry: negative_findings 'Allergies' absent. (b) allergy with status uncertain, the substance as described, the reaction if said, plus an allergy_uncertain uncertainty. (c) allergy with the reaction. (d) nothing at all. NEVER list a medicine the patient has taken without a reaction as an allergy, and the plan must not prescribe a drug of a recorded allergy's family.

features: third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.
doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.

omissions.text: Periods are light as well as not painful.
Last menstrual period was approximately 6 weeks ago, though the patient was unsure of the exact date.
Patient denied taking any daily medications; only took one Crocin last month for headache, not regularly.
Patient specifically reported tolerance of penicillin/amoxicillin with no rash or other reaction after amoxicillin last year for throat infection.
Doctor initially proposed starting cyproterone 2 mg with ethinylestradiol (Diane), 1 tablet daily for 21 days then a break.
The reason the combined pill was not started was history of headaches with visual aura ('sparkly zigzag lights'), making it unsuitable.
Pelvic ultrasound was described as lower-abdomen gel only, with no needle.
Nurse instructed that fasting means only water from tonight.
Additional family history: mother had diabetes in pregnancy (gestational diabetes), as reported by caregiver.
Negative surgical history: no past operations other than wisdom tooth extraction/nothing major.
Doctor noted that abdomen was not examined today.
